Here's the post — swap in your own name where it says [Your Name]:

---

The Winter School on Elliptic Curves and Modular Forms ended on Saturday, and we owe a lot of thanks.

We, [Your Name], Ketaki Joglekar and Faizan Mirza, organised it along with our faculty mentor Prof. Anuradha Venkatesan, who backed the idea from the start, pushed us to apply for the grant and read every draft of the schedule. We met in Seminar Hall 2, Department of Mathematics, Sahyadri Institute of Science, Pune, from 5 to 7 November, and it was a genuinely serious three days: 112 applications, 41 participants (MSc and early PhD) from 9 states, selected on a statement of interest plus one reference.

The Rs 2.4 lakh from the Institute's student initiative grant paid for hostel stay and travel for 18 outstation students, which for several of them is the only reason they could be here at all.

Thank you to our speakers:
• Dr. Nilesh Dharmadhikari (Hyderabad) on Mordell–Weil groups
• Dr. Sunanda Iyer (Chennai) on modular forms
• Dr. Tomasz Wierzbicki (online from Kraków) on computations in Sage

On day two, the power went for nearly two hours in the afternoon and most of our laptops died. We moved the problem session to the canteen, pulled out two rolling whiteboards, and carried on. People kept telling us afterwards that it was the best session of the three days, so that unplanned hour is now one of our favourite memories.

A special mention for the MSc student from Silchar who found an error in a worked example in Sunanda ma'am's notes. She corrected it live and thanked him on the spot, which is exactly the kind of thing this format should make possible.

Also thank you to Mr. Prakash Salunke in our office, who sorted out hostel rooms at 11 pm when the booking fell through, and to the six PhD student volunteers who ran the problem sessions and the logistics. That format worked well and we intend to keep it.

For our MSc students, a small school like this matters more than a big conference. Here you can actually ask questions, and they get answered.

Slides and problem sheets will go up on the department website within two weeks.

We hope to run a second edition in late 2027, if the grant comes through. Thank you to the 41 participants, our speakers, our mentor, and everyone else who made it work.
